# Source fixture provenance

Captured September 5, 2026 by ordinary, bounded HTTPS public reads. No source access controls were bypassed. These are parser excerpts, **not complete snapshots**.

- `ca-list.html`: first three report rows and complete pagination controls from https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/databreach/list. Real source values and IDs retained; unrelated markup and later rows removed. Original response SHA-256 `341aebc43fb9e35f7f2ede09226c73990ea4187c98c8a7ae58d9939fc08d9ce4`.
- `hhs-navigation.html`: public “View HIPAA Breach Reports” command link from https://ocrportal.hhs.gov/ocr/breach/breach_frontpage.jsf. Reduced form wrapper; view state replaced by `fixture-only` and session suffix removed. The link itself is captured markup.
- `hhs-reports.html`: report table container from the resulting https://ocrportal.hhs.gov/ocr/breach/breach_report_hip.jsf response, first three real report rows retained. Pagination display changed from `1 - 100` to `1 - 3` to match fixture size; source total of 733 retained. Original response SHA-256 `60cca42151531e432cdf0ccdaeef6bd9262ddb4190a9b71a715dac3668ede123`.
- `hhs-page2.xml`: first two real rows (source offsets 100 and 101) returned by normal PrimeFaces public pagination. Non-table updates removed; view state replaced by `fixture-state`. Original response SHA-256 `f49b2da4f0d7bfa78c4698bd9d16748bfe14dec8b9b725300ec2f62df62762bd`.
- `ma-tables-synthetic.json`: explicitly synthetic pdfplumber-style rows based on the documented legacy Massachusetts column contract, with reordered headers, a continuation page, and year rollover. The official Massachusetts index returned HTTP 403; no annual report PDF was fetched. These tests validate row normalization and discovery logic only; they do **not** establish current live PDF extraction fidelity.

Synthetic mutations made inside tests cover errors, malformed values, and response boundaries. No tests perform network calls. Public CA full CSV endpoint timed out during a 30-second read; the adapter uses linked HTML listing pages with stable native `sb24` IDs, defaults to a bounded 120-page window, accepts an explicit 1–200 page limit, and marks truncation or unverified pagination partial. HHS captures only the **HIPAA Under Investigation** view, excluding Archive and Part 2.

MA PDF coverage regressions additionally use mocked pdfplumber pages with synthetic text/table omissions. A page without extracted tables, a disagreement in native IDs, or unheaded multi-column rows fails collection. Agreement between extracted text and tables is only an omission check: the current live collector remains partial because an independent annual source-count feed has not been validated. No new live PDF claim is established by these tests.

`ca-last.html` was captured by a normal public read of https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/databreach/list?page=105 on September 5, 2026. The actual final page has 45 rows and active page106/previous-page controls; the fixture retains its first three rows and complete pager. Original SHA-256 `fbd9c48213b2a810938e6406633c33e572c71575ed4f658e76ebfd9b1857ec70`. Reverified first+last pages establish 106 pages and 5,295 listed reports at observation time; they do not alone prove every intermediate page.

The official 2026 Massachusetts PDF search-index excerpt includes native ID `2026-1146` and reported date `15-Jul-26`; this date-format regression uses the indexed spelling. Both the official index and independently discovered https://www.mass.gov/doc/data-breach-report-2026/download returned HTTP403 on recheck. Search-cache counts conflict and are not used as completeness evidence. No downloaded PDF fixture exists.

## Texas and SEC special portals (September 5, 2026)

- `texas-navigation.html` retains the official public page's declared `DataSecurityReports.getDatareports(false)` read action. Page-state/CSRF/authorization fields are replaced with fixture placeholders. This is the same action used to populate the visible table, not an administrative API.
- `texas-response.json` contains the first three records from the successful public action response, reduced to fields rendered by the public table plus native identifiers. All 625 current public-version records were returned in one response, and all 625 had unique Salesforce IDs. Original response SHA-256 `b91ac0b7ec0505fd12e5a8b4c4896c891dbdbc9d2d0946c856c4b07882a6acdc`; 542,857 response bytes. The first protocol attempt omitted the normal page Referer and received explicit RPC status402; including the actual landing-page Referer reproduced the public client call successfully. No login or privileged endpoints were used.
- `sec-feed-synthetic.xml` and `sec-index-synthetic.html` are **synthetic**, not captures. An ordinary request to the actual SEC current Atom feed using the project identity returned HTTP403; access attempts stopped. The tests exercise accession identity, actual document links, Item1.05 filtering, and valid zero-match accounting, but do not establish live SEC parser compatibility. No XBRL instance URL is guessed or required. A genuine optional `SEC_USER_AGENT` value can replace the project default; no email address is invented.

Texas counts are explicitly Texans affected. API fields not rendered by the public table—including broader total counts and additional dates—are excluded from collection and fixture records. Raw transient navigation tokens never enter the public export.
